messages:
carla_support: Hey — nightly canary deploys started failing around 02:10 with 401s during artifact upload. Happens ~7m into the job every time. No recent deploy changes AFAIK. Logs: `upload failed: 401 unauthorized` and `token expired` in the proxy.
ashley_infra: Thanks, looking. Is this only on the self-hosted runners or GH hosted too?
carla_support: Only our self-hosted fleet (gha-runner-*) — GH-hosted unaffected. One example run: workflow run/112233, runner gha-runner-5.
mike_sre: Can you paste the proxy logs for that run? ci-proxy tends to log token mint + cache keys.
carla_support: pastebin: https://paste.redwood/abc123 — see entries around `2026-03-17T02:03:45Z`.
linh_devex: quick skim: I see ci-proxy minted a short-lived SA token (ttl=300s) and then later reused a cached token for another job, which then expired mid-upload.
ashley_infra: Wait, TTL 300s? Our tokens usually 900s for GH runner flows. Did something change in the signer config?
ci-proxy-bot: automated-note: token_request(serviceAccount=ci-deployer@redwood-prod, scopes=[storage.read, storage.write], ttl=300s) -> issued. CacheKey=sa:ci-deployer|scope:storage.read,storage.write
mike_sre: That cache key looks suspicious — it's missing job/audience/job-id. If two jobs request different audiences but same scope+sa, proxy might reuse older token for new job.
linh_devex: Repro steps I ran: 1) start job A requesting upload scope; token minted; 2) start job B with same sa but narrower audience and longer runtime; ci-proxy returned cached token from A; token expired in B causing 401. Seen locally with two parallel runners.
carla_support: So this is a bug in token cache keying in ci-proxy, not IAM policy changes. Any quick mitigation for prod Canary tonight?
ashley_infra: Temporary mitigations: - set CI_PROXY_DISABLE_TOKEN_CACHE=1 on runner pool; or bump token ttl to 1800s via signer override for `ci-deployer` (but prefer cache fix). I can flip disable-cache flag on gha-runner-5 pool now.
mike_sre: I'll push a hotfix branch that includes job-id and audience in cache key and add tests. Will roll to canary then prod.
linh_devex: Patch includes: `cacheKey := fmt.Sprintf("sa:%s|scopes:%s|aud:%s|job:%s", sa, scopesHash, audience, jobID)` and new unit test for parallel requests.
ci-proxy-bot: deploy-batch: ci-proxy v1.12.3-hotfix -> canary (gha-runner-canary) started
deploy-bot: rolling canary to 5 runners, monitoring artifact uploads.
ashley_infra: Can confirm: after disabling cache on the affected pool, the two parallel jobs completed without 401s. Uploads stable.
carla_support: Thanks all — can you file a follow-up to ensure we increase default ttl only if needed? Also want a postmortem on why signer default changed to 300s (if it did).
mike_sre: Filed: https://issues.redwood/INFR-4826 with root cause, mitigation, and rollout plan. Will revert cache-disable once hotfix is verified.
linh_devex: Timeline: hotfix merged + canary ok -> rollout to prod within 2 hours. Also adding telemetry: token-age metric to alert if >75% of TTL.
carla_support: OK closing the support ticket once prod rollout done. :thumbsup:
